verdict_explanation: This loop closed the third of PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs's four originally-merged concerns (store-name resolution, now Services/Stores/StoreNameLookup.cs) with a pure, build-verified relocation - real progress on the churn-flagged god-class, and true-external network calls (GOG/Epic/Ubisoft) are no longer instantiated inside the UI class. Two concerns (UI event handling, backup/restore orchestration) and F3/F4 remain open, keeping the review at this verdict rather than a stronger one.

architecture_quality.proof: PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs shrank from 2,530 to 2,299 LOC (231 lines, -9%) this loop: GetGogGameNameAsync, GetEpicGameNameAsync, LoadUbisoftGameListAsync, GetUbisoftGameNameAsync, FindGameByNameAsync, NormaliseGameName, and their four cache fields moved to the new Services/Stores/StoreNameLookup.cs:1-263, closing the third of the original four merged concerns. Two concerns remain merged (RestoreBackupCoreAsync at :2158-2241, UI event handling), keeping this a partial-credit move within Middling territory.

state_management.proof: Unaffected by this loop's change. AppliedArtworkStore's lock symmetry (resolved loop 2) and isLibraryOperationRunning unchanged; write-authority for the relocated caches is unchanged (still one caller, LoadGameEntriesAsync).

domain_modeling.proof: Unaffected by this loop's change; SteamGridDbClient.ParseOfficialCapsuleUrl (SteamGridDbClient.cs:144-199) still hand-parsed outside the DTO's own deserialization, verified unchanged this loop.

data_flow.proof: GOG/Epic/Ubisoft true-external network calls are no longer instantiated inside PrimaryWidget - moved to Services/Stores/StoreNameLookup.cs, which owns its own HttpClient field (StoreNameLookup.cs:37-39), mirroring the established EpicLibrary.cs pattern in the same directory. No port/interface introduced, so this stays below the 7-anchor; one fewer file to read to trace a true-external dependency.

framework_idioms.proof: Unaffected by this loop's change. The two JSON idioms (DataContractJsonSerializer vs. ad hoc Windows.Data.Json) still coexist, verbatim, in both the old and new locations.

concurrency.proof: Unaffected by this loop's change. F3's fully sequential per-game round-trips (PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs:324-741) remain open; the four store-name caches are still plain, non-thread-safe Dictionary (now on StoreNameLookup, same non-thread-safety as before the move).

simplicity.proof: Store-name-resolution logic for all three stores now lives in one 263-line file (Services/Stores/StoreNameLookup.cs) instead of interleaved inside a 2,500-line UI class; a reader tracing that one behavior reads one dedicated file. No new abstraction, protocol, or ceremony added - reuses the exact existing code. Not a bigger jump because F4's duplicate lazy-cache skeleton is untouched and the new file has a residual asymmetry (see Finding #1).

test_strategy.proof: No test project exists; standing user instruction prohibits adding one this run. Verified unchanged this loop (no *.csproj matching a test name found; SteamGridDB.Xbox.sln project list unchanged). Named, non-backlog-item blocker, as recorded loops 1-2.

credibility.proof: The three store-name-resolution methods still swallow failures via Debug.WriteLine only - this loop moved that code verbatim (same swallow pattern, same shape, just relocated), so the cited weakness persists unchanged in its new location (StoreNameLookup.cs:66-69,150-153,216-219,239-242,269-272).

authority_map.concern: Store-name resolution caches (gogNameCache, epicNameCache, nameMatchCache, ubisoftGameLookupCache)

The official-artwork gate (FindOfficialLookalikeAsync, PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs:1436-1507) is a narrow, evidence-tuned veto whose code comments cite the specific regression case and slack margin that motivated it. Re-verified unchanged this loop (line numbers shifted by -8 from the field-block removal near the top of the file; content unaffected).

This loop's extraction mirrors EpicLibrary.cs's existing shape (a plain internal static class in Services/Stores/, no interface, no DI) rather than inventing a new pattern for the fourth store-facing lookup type added to that directory.

findings.title: PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs still merges UI event handling and backup/restore orchestration behind zero Interface boundary
findings.why_it_matters: The churn-flagged god-class (21 edits, still the largest file in the repo) continues to bundle two structurally distinct concerns with no Module boundary between them, so a change to either risks touching the other.
findings.what_is_wrong: UI event handling (the *_Click handlers, grid/search panel management, artwork download/replace flow) and backup/restore orchestration (RestoreBackupCoreAsync, RestoreBackupAsync, the RestoreBackupResult enum) remain private members on one 2,299-line Page-derived class with no Interface separating them. Store-name resolution (GetGogGameNameAsync, GetEpicGameNameAsync, LoadUbisoftGameListAsync, GetUbisoftGameNameAsync, FindGameByNameAsync, NormaliseGameName, plus the four cache fields) was extracted to Services/Stores/StoreNameLookup.cs this loop, closing the third of the four original concerns (artwork ranking was the first, closed loop 1).
evidence: SteamGridDB.Xbox/Services/Stores/StoreNameLookup.cs:1-263 (new file this loop - store-name resolution now has its own Module)

SteamGridDB.Xbox/Services/Stores/StoreNameLookup.cs:27-28 (gogNameCache/epicNameCache are internal fields written and read only by PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs, not by StoreNameLookup itself - residual split ownership, see Deepening Candidates)
findings.leverage_impact: Every future backup/restore fix or UI change still touches the same file; a maintainer touching either risks disturbing the other via shared Dispatcher/StatusText plumbing.
findings.locality_impact: A maintainer fixing a UI bug still reads through ~2,300 lines including unrelated backup/restore logic to find the relevant lines - narrower than before (was ~2,530 including store-name resolution too) but still spread across two concerns.
findings.metric_signal: PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs: 2,299 LOC (re-measured this loop, down from 2,530 at loop 2's end) - 231 lines / 9% smaller after this loop's extraction.
findings.why_weakens_submission: Ownership of the two remaining distinct concerns (UI event handling, backup/restore orchestration) is still untraceable from any single Module; the file is smaller but not yet at the one-or-two-shallow-wrapper bar the architecture-quality 7-anchor requires.
findings.minimal_correction_path: Backup/restore orchestration is the next self-contained candidate, though it is more entangled with UI (Dispatcher.RunAsync, StatusText, EntriesSharingImage) than store-name resolution was - extracting it cleanly needs either a UI-update callback parameter or accepting a partial split. Do not attempt the same mechanical-move shape without first confirming which Dispatcher.RunAsync blocks can move to the caller without changing update timing.

change: a new file for backup/restore (if pursued) OR Services/Stores/StoreNameLookup.cs (if the split-cache residual is pursued instead)

findings.title: Library load issues one sequential SteamGridDB round-trip per game with no bounded concurrency
findings.why_it_matters: Load time scales linearly with library size and network latency on the widget's primary open path - the one flow every user hits every time.
findings.what_is_wrong: The gameCache foreach loop in LoadGameEntriesAsync awaits sgdbClient.GetGameByPlatformIdAsync (and the GOG/Epic/Ubisoft name fallbacks, now routed through StoreNameLookup) one game at a time; nothing overlaps the independent per-game network calls.
evidence: SteamGridDB.Xbox/PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs:324-741 (per-folder, per-entry foreach; awaits GetGameByPlatformIdAsync at :577 and the StoreNameLookup fallbacks at :601,623,638,658, with nothing overlapped - re-verified at current line numbers this loop after F1's extraction shifted them)
findings.leverage_impact: There is only one call site (the load loop); a future second caller of the same pattern would inherit the same linear cost with no leverage from batching, since none exists.
findings.locality_impact: The fix is local to LoadGameEntriesAsync's loop body and StoreNameLookup's cache field declarations; it does not need to spread to callers.
findings.metric_signal: One HTTP round-trip per game per store lookup; a 100-game library issues 100+ sequential requests with no overlap (D2, lens-efficiency.md).
findings.why_weakens_submission: Structural waste on the widget's primary hot path. The fix is well-understood (bounded concurrency) but crosses a real risk boundary: the four store-name caches (now on StoreNameLookup) are still not thread-safe and currently rely on this exact sequencing to stay race-free.
findings.minimal_correction_path: Bound concurrency (e.g. SemaphoreSlim(4-8) + Task.WhenAll) around the per-entry body, and switch StoreNameLookup's gogNameCache/epicNameCache/nameMatchCache/ubisoftGameLookupCache to ConcurrentDictionary before parallelizing - do not parallelize without that change, or the caches race.

findings.title: Hand-rolled double-checked-locking cache pattern duplicated between AppliedArtworkStore and EpicLibrary
findings.why_it_matters: The same ~25-line lazy-load-with-gate skeleton was written twice by hand instead of once; a future third cache (the store-name caches in F1/F3) would make it three.
findings.what_is_wrong: AppliedArtworkStore.LoadAsync (AppliedArtworkStore.cs:95-147) and EpicLibrary.LoadAsync (EpicLibrary.cs:67-89) both implement: check-null, await SemaphoreSlim gate, re-check-null, populate, release - identical structure, no shared helper. Unaffected by this loop's fix, which targeted store-name resolution in a different file (StoreNameLookup.cs's LoadUbisoftGameListAsync uses a simpler unlocked lazy-init, not this pattern, so no third copy was introduced).
findings.leverage_impact: A shared lazy-cache primitive would pay for itself across at least these two call sites.
findings.locality_impact: Today a bug in the locking pattern must be fixed in two places; a shared helper collapses that to one.
findings.why_weakens_submission: Duplicate concurrency boilerplate is exactly the kind of copy-paste-with-slight-variation the leaf-module duplication sweep looks for; it is real but contained.
findings.minimal_correction_path: Extract a small internal AsyncLazy-style helper (check-lock-recheck-populate) that both call sites construct against. Do not add an interface or DI - this is one concrete type serving two internal call sites, not a Seam.

simplification_check.structurally_necessary: Moving store-name-resolution methods and their four cache fields out of PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs into Services/Stores/StoreNameLookup.cs - closes the third of F1's four merged concerns; the smallest honest fix is a pure relocation, reusing the exact code (no new abstraction, no new ceremony).
simplification_check.helpful_simplification: Reader locality for "how does the widget resolve a third-party store's game name" improved from "search a 2,500-line UI file" to "read one 263-line file."
simplification_check.should_not_be_done: Encapsulating the GOG/Epic caching logic inside StoreNameLookup this loop - the original code's cache-hit/cache-miss branching treats an empty cached value as "needs refetch" (PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs:599); a naive wrapper method that returns on any cache hit (including empty) would silently change retry behavior with no test oracle to catch the difference. Deferred to a Deepening Candidate.
simplification_check.tests_after_fix: No test project exists (standing instruction); MSBuild compile is the only regression oracle. This is a pure code-motion refactor - Meta-Rule 4 does not apply: no isolation/Sendable/conditional-compilation/cross-file-visibility/lock-ordering boundary was crossed. Visibility was deliberately widened (private to internal), not narrowed, for exactly the two fields that need cross-file access.

deepening_candidates.source_friction_proven: Finding F1's residual evidence - gogNameCache/epicNameCache are internal fields on StoreNameLookup (StoreNameLookup.cs:27-28) written and read only by PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs (:597-613, :616-630), while nameMatchCache/ubisoftGameLookupCache (same class) are private and owned internally.
deepening_candidates.why_shallow_or_misplaced: gogNameCache/epicNameCache expose internal mutable state as a bare Interface (a Dictionary directly, not a method) - Interface approx Implementation for that slice, the shallow-module test's own definition of shallow.
deepening_candidates.behavior_to_move_behind_interface: The check-cache/fetch/populate-cache logic currently inline in LoadGameEntriesAsync (PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs:597-613, :616-630) should become GetOrFetchGogNameAsync/GetOrFetchEpicNameAsync methods on StoreNameLookup, mirroring GetUbisoftGameNameAsync's shape, with gogNameCache/epicNameCache becoming private.
deepening_candidates.test_surface_after_change: none (no test project; build-verified only, same as today)
deepening_candidates.smallest_first_step: Port GOG's caching first - it has no secondary fallback source to preserve (Epic's path also calls EpicLibrary.GetDisplayNameAsync first via ??, a second thing the wrapper must get right).
deepening_candidates.what_not_to_do: Do not change the "empty cached value still means refetch" semantics (PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs:599) while doing this - a wrapper that treats any cache hit (including an empty one) as final would silently change retry behavior.

builder_notes.pattern: A mechanical move (relocate code, qualify call sites) is a different, safer class of refactor than an encapsulating move (relocate code AND change how callers use it) - only the first is safe without a test oracle.
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: If the fix can be described as "cut these lines, paste them in a new file, add a class-name prefix at each call site" with the pasted lines byte-identical to the original, it is mechanical. If describing the fix requires "and now the caller doesn't need to check X first," it is encapsulating - a different, higher-risk category.
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: In a codebase with no test suite, prefer the mechanical move now and file the encapsulating move as a Deepening Candidate with its behavior-preservation trap named explicitly.
builder_notes.stack_example: C# - this loop moved GetGogGameNameAsync verbatim into StoreNameLookup.cs (mechanical) but explicitly deferred folding gogNameCache's check-then-fetch logic into the same class (encapsulating - the empty-string-means-refetch branch in PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs:599 is easy to flatten incorrectly).

builder_notes.pattern: Extracting one slice of a multi-concern god-class narrows Locality for the extracted concern immediately, even before the whole file is broken up.
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: A single file's method list spans several unrelated verb groups (fetch, parse, click-handle, restore) with no sub-namespacing; pick the verb group with the fewest external dependencies as the first slice - it is the lowest-risk mechanical move.
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: Rank remaining god-class slices by how many UI/framework types (Dispatcher, StatusText, view-bound collections) their methods touch; extract the zero-UI-dependency slices first.

builder_notes.pattern: Churn concentrates where concerns are merged (unchanged from loops 1-2 - still live, now measuring a smaller file).
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: One file dominates the six-month edit count and is several times larger than everything else, even after partial extraction.
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: When a file's edit count and size both dominate the repo, extract the concern that changed rather than adding to the pile.

narrative: Place, not win. This loop closed the third of PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs's four originally-merged concerns with a pure, build-verified relocation - no new abstraction, no new ceremony, the moved code byte-identical to its source. architecture_quality and data_flow both moved up on structural proof, and code_simplicity improved because store-name resolution now has a single dedicated file to read. But PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs still merges UI event handling and backup/restore orchestration with no Interface boundary (F1, still Serious), LoadGameEntriesAsync still issues one sequential network round-trip per game (F3), the duplicate lazy-cache skeleton (F4) is untouched, and this loop's own fix leaves a smaller residual (two of StoreNameLookup's four cache fields are owned-in-name-only by that class). Runtime ownership remains trustworthy for what has been resolved; concurrency is not yet trustworthy (F3 open). Tests remain absent by standing instruction. Future work risks overengineering specifically at the noted Deepening Candidate: folding GOG/Epic caching into StoreNameLookup needs the empty-cache-means-refetch semantics preserved exactly.

loop_result.what_changed: Moved store-name-resolution methods (GetGogGameNameAsync, GetEpicGameNameAsync, LoadUbisoftGameListAsync, GetUbisoftGameNameAsync, FindGameByNameAsync, NormaliseGameName) and their four cache fields out of PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs into a new Services/Stores/StoreNameLookup.cs, qualifying the five call sites in LoadGameEntriesAsync with the new class name; registered the new file in SteamGridDB.Xbox.csproj.
loop_result.evidence_change_is_honest: MSBuild (the sole regression oracle per Discovery - no test project exists) passed clean both before and after the change (exit 0 both times, same command as loops 1-2's baseline). git diff --stat: PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs (8 insertions, 239 deletions), SteamGridDB.Xbox.csproj (+1 line), Services/Stores/StoreNameLookup.cs (new, 263 lines). The diff is a pure move with one disclosed, mechanical field-reference edit: five of the six moved method bodies are byte-identical to their pre-move source; the three methods that call GOG/Epic/Ubisoft (GetGogGameNameAsync, GetEpicGameNameAsync, LoadUbisoftGameListAsync) have their sharedHttpClient reference changed to httpClient, a new dedicated field on StoreNameLookup, so a Services/Stores type does not depend back on the UI class for a shared instance. The qualifying StoreNameLookup. prefix was also added at the five call sites. This changes which HttpClient object instance issues the same three store-lookup HTTP calls, not the number of calls, retry behavior, or selection semantics - confirmed by the independent implementation-reviewer pass (verdict: approved; reality/honesty/regression all passed), which flagged the earlier 'byte-identical' phrasing as understating this disclosed edit; corrected here.

implementation_review.reason: The six named methods and four cache fields are verifiably gone from PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs and correctly relocated to StoreNameLookup.cs with all call sites properly qualified, the move is honest (method bodies match except a disclosed, behavior-neutral HttpClient field swap and the deliberate private-to-internal widening), and no same-or-higher-severity regression was introduced by the move itself.
regressions: StoreNameLookup.cs:27-28 - gogNameCache/epicNameCache are internal fields whose check-cache/fetch/populate logic still lives outside the class (PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs:597-613,616-630) - a partial shallow-module residue introduced by this loop's split; already self-disclosed as Finding F1 evidence and a Deepening Candidate, lower severity than the targeted Serious finding.

StoreNameLookup.cs:37-39 - a second static HttpClient singleton now exists alongside PrimaryWidget's sharedHttpClient (PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs:73); functionally inert (no custom config on either instance), but the loop's original evidence_change_is_honest text overstated the moved methods as fully byte-identical when 3 of 6 had their HttpClient field reference changed - corrected in this artifact.
